# Sentido de Pertenencia: Sense of Place (SP)

Sense of Place (also called Sentido de Pertenencia) is the equal weight arithmetic mean of three subgoals:

1. **CCE**: Coastal Community Engagement
2. **LSP**: Lasting Special Places
3. **ICO**: Iconic Species

This October 2026 script is a deliberate update of `sp_current_status.qmd`. I am keeping the older script as-is and writing the revised aggregation here so we can compare safely.

**What changed for this update**

1. **CCE is NA for now.** After EWG 3.2, we restructured CCE around civic, educational, and social engagement with the Gulf (see `CCE/(SP) CCE Finalizing Methods (3).pdf`). Until we have comparable region-wide data for that framework, publishing a CCE number from one or two incomplete layers would not be representative. Setting CCE to NA does **not** mean engagement is absent; it means we do not yet have fair data for the subgoal as we now define it. Perception of security / safety is **not** included in CCE.
2. **ICO uses the expert-final Keep list** from `ICO/v2026_expert_final_093026`, written as `ico_mean_risk_status_per_region_093026.csv`.
3. **LSP uses the v2026 merge** from `LSP/v2026/script8_merge.qmd`, written as `lsp_goal_current_status_by_region.csv`, with raw scores for **2020 and 2023**. I then expand those assessment-year scores into an annual series for **2018-2025** to match the ICO years (carry-forward and linear interpolation between SIMEC years; see below).

So for Index 1.1 right now, Sense of Place is the arithmetic mean of LSP and ICO only. CCE still appears in the table as NA so the three-subgoal structure stays visible.

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(here)
library(plotly)

rgn_labels <- c(
  "Region_1" = "Western Upper Gulf",
  "Region_2" = "Western Midriff Islands",
  "Region_3" = "Western Central Gulf",
  "Region_4" = "Western Southern Gulf",
  "Region_5" = "Eastern Upper Gulf",
  "Region_6" = "Eastern Midriff Islands",
  "Region_7" = "Southern Sonora Coast",
  "Region_8" = "Sinaloa Coast",
  "Region_9" = "Southeastern Gulf"
)

rgn_colors <- c(
  "Region_1" = "#C03729",
  "Region_2" = "#E68C7C",
  "Region_3" = "#FC8F24",
  "Region_4" = "#dcaa38",
  "Region_5" = "#cbd2a0",
  "Region_6" = "#98a25a",
  "Region_7" = "#747428",
  "Region_8" = "#627391",
  "Region_9" = "#8d61a9"
)

region_levels <- paste0("Region_", 1:9)
rgn_label_colors <- setNames(unname(rgn_colors[region_levels]), unname(rgn_labels[region_levels]))
```

# Coastal Community Engagement (CCE) — NA for now

I am not aggregating Ama tu Playa, cultural places, NGOs, or security into a CCE score in this script. Those layers can still live in supplementary materials, but the scored CCE subgoal is NA until the civic / educational / social framework has enough comparable data. Safety is intentionally left out.

```{r}
# placeholder cce "scores": all regions and sp years, status na
sp_years <- 2018:2025

cce_current_status <- tidyr::crossing(
  rgn_id = region_levels,
  year = sp_years
) %>%
  mutate(
    current_status = NA_real_,
    reason = "cce restructured after ewg 3.2; na until civic/educational/social data are comparable; safety not included"
  ) %>%
  arrange(rgn_id, year)

cce_current_status
```

```{r}
write_csv(
  cce_current_status,
  here::here(
    "/home/shares/ohi/OHI_GOC/goal_prep/sp/cce/v2026/output",
    "cce_current_status_Oct2026_NA.csv"
  )
)
```

# Lasting Special Places (LSP) and Iconic Species (ICO)

I will bring in the finished LSP and ICO outputs from the October-updated pipelines.

## LSP assessment years, then annual expansion

SIMEC-based LSP is scored for **2020 and 2023**. To build a continuous series that matches ICO (**2018-2025**), I treat those as the only observed assessment years and fill the rest as follows:

- **2018-2020**: use the 2020 current status (carry the first assessment back so earlier years are not blank).
- **2021-2022**: linearly interpolate between the 2020 and 2023 current status scores.
- **2023-2025**: use the 2023 current status (carry forward until the next SIMEC release).

When the **2026 SIMEC** scores are released, I will change the post-2023 rule so that **2024-2025** are interpolated between 2023 and 2026, and 2026 onward carries the new assessment. For now there is no 2026 score, so 2023-2025 stay at the 2023 value.

```{r}
# lasting special places: 2020 and 2023 from lsp/v2026 script8_merge
lsp_assessment <- read_csv(here::here(
  "/home/shares/ohi/OHI_GOC/goal_prep/sp/lsp/v2026/output",
  "lsp_goal_current_status_by_region.csv"
)) %>%
  mutate(rgn_id = str_replace_all(rgn_id, " ", "_")) %>%
  dplyr::select(rgn_id, year, lsp_status = current_status)

colnames(lsp_assessment)
unique(lsp_assessment$year) # expect 2020 and 2023
lsp_assessment

lsp_wide <- lsp_assessment %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = year, values_from = lsp_status, names_prefix = "lsp_")

# expand to 2018-2025 with carry-forward and linear interpolation between 2020 and 2023
lsp_current_status <- tidyr::crossing(
  rgn_id = region_levels,
  year = sp_years
) %>%
  left_join(lsp_wide, by = "rgn_id") %>%
  mutate(
    lsp_status = case_when(
      year <= 2020 ~ lsp_2020,
      year >= 2023 ~ lsp_2023,
      TRUE ~ lsp_2020 + ((year - 2020) / (2023 - 2020)) * (lsp_2023 - lsp_2020)
    ),
    lsp_method = case_when(
      year <= 2020 ~ "carry 2020 assessment",
      year >= 2023 ~ "carry 2023 assessment (until 2026 simec)",
      TRUE ~ "linear interpolate 2020 to 2023"
    )
  ) %>%
  dplyr::select(rgn_id, year, lsp_status, lsp_method)

lsp_current_status

# quick check: 2020 and 2023 match the assessment table
lsp_current_status %>%
  filter(year %in% c(2020, 2023)) %>%
  left_join(lsp_assessment, by = c("rgn_id", "year"), suffix = c("", "_raw")) %>%
  summarise(max_abs_diff = max(abs(lsp_status - lsp_status_raw), na.rm = TRUE))
```

```{r}
write_csv(
  lsp_current_status,
  here::here(
    "/home/shares/ohi/OHI_GOC/goal_prep/sp/lsp/v2026/output",
    "lsp_goal_current_status_by_region_annual_2018_2025_Oct2026.csv"
  )
)
```

## ICO annual series

```{r}
# iconic species: expert-final keep list from ico/v2026_expert_final_093026
ico_current_status <- read_csv(here::here(
  "/home/shares/ohi/OHI_GOC/goal_prep/sp/ico/output",
  "ico_mean_risk_status_per_region_093026.csv"
)) %>%
  mutate(rgn_id = str_replace_all(rgn_id, " ", "_")) %>%
  dplyr::select(rgn_id, year, ico_status = current_status)

colnames(ico_current_status)

# keep the same years as the expanded lsp / sp series
ico_for_sp <- ico_current_status %>%
  filter(year %in% sp_years)

ico_for_sp
```

# Sense of Place (SP) aggregation across subgoals

Because CCE is NA, Sense of Place is currently the equal-weight average of the expanded LSP series and ICO for 2018-2025. I still join CCE so the column stays in the output as NA.

```{r}
sp_joined <- lsp_current_status %>%
  dplyr::select(rgn_id, year, lsp_status) %>%
  full_join(ico_for_sp, by = c("rgn_id", "year")) %>%
  full_join(
    cce_current_status %>% dplyr::select(rgn_id, year, cce_status = current_status),
    by = c("rgn_id", "year")
  ) %>%
  arrange(rgn_id, year)

sp_current_status <- sp_joined %>%
  filter(year %in% sp_years) %>%
  mutate(
    current_status = rowMeans(
      cbind(cce_status, lsp_status, ico_status),
      na.rm = TRUE
    )
  ) %>%
  dplyr::select(rgn_id, year, current_status, cce_status, lsp_status, ico_status)

sp_current_status

# quick check that cce is entirely na and sp is the mean of lsp and ico
sp_current_status %>%
  summarise(
    n_rows = n(),
    n_years = n_distinct(year),
    n_cce_na = sum(is.na(cce_status)),
    mean_abs_diff_from_lsp_ico_mean = mean(
      abs(current_status - rowMeans(cbind(lsp_status, ico_status), na.rm = TRUE)),
      na.rm = TRUE
    )
  )
```

# Quick look

I will plot the expanded LSP series (2018-2025), ICO, and the final SP current status by region. I am not plotting a CCE score because it is NA on purpose.

```{r}
lsp_plot <- lsp_current_status %>%
  mutate(region_label = rgn_labels[rgn_id])

ico_plot <- ico_for_sp %>%
  mutate(region_label = rgn_labels[rgn_id])

sp_plot <- sp_current_status %>%
  mutate(region_label = rgn_labels[rgn_id])
```

## LSP

```{r}
lsp_plotly <- plotly::plot_ly(
  lsp_plot,
  x = ~year,
  y = ~lsp_status,
  color = ~region_label,
  colors = rgn_label_colors,
  type = "scatter",
  mode = "lines+markers"
) %>%
  layout(
    title = "CURRENT STATUS: Lasting Special Places (LSP; 2018-2025 expanded from 2020 and 2023)",
    xaxis = list(title = "Año // Year", dtick = 1),
    yaxis = list(title = "Puntaje // Percent (out of 100)")
  ) %>%
  add_lines(
    x = range(lsp_plot$year, na.rm = TRUE),
    y = c(100, 100),
    line = list(color = "black", width = 2, dash = "dash"),
    name = "Meta // Goal (100/100)",
    inherit = FALSE
  )

lsp_plotly
```
